problems: The 'sun' is a flat, unshaded white disc in every frame (storyboard 2-16, all three full frames). It has no surface, no rolling and no sense of volume, so it reads as a blown-out sprite rather than an object sliding over grass.

Storyboard frames 5-6 and the 25% frame: the disc passes straight through the sheep and the blue figure. The sheep and the pig behind it neither move nor get pushed, so it looks like clipping, not contact.

'Among my friends': once the sun has landed (storyboard 6-12, 50% frame), the crab, the blue figure and the sheep stand frozen beside a glowing ball. Their faces stay mostly dark even at arm's length. 'Nobody kicked it' covers the missing kick, but not the fact that nobody reacts at all.
'It slid': nothing visible starts or drives the slide. The ground looks flat, and the ball drifts toward the camera with no push and no slope to explain it.
'Through a bush' (storyboard 13-14, 75% frame): the bush leaves cut through the disc and the bush doesn't bend or move. It reads as two meshes overlapping, not something going through.

'Toward the sea': you never clearly see the sea. In storyboard 16 there is only a dark teal sliver at the bottom left, and a huge dark green blob covers the right third of the frame, as if the camera ran into foliage.
The camera trails the ball and keeps it low in the frame. The friends get small and drift into the background from storyboard 9 on, so the 'among my friends' part is lost for most of the film.
posts.critique: A falling sun that lights the grass is a lovely idea, and the yellow pool of light really works. But the ball is a flat white disc that clips through the sheep and the bush, slides with no cause and ends against a blob of foliage instead of the sea. The caption promises more contact and place than the film shows.
